placementGuidelines: A hummingbird-favorite Agastache cultivar, frequently mixed up at nurseries with the unrelated groundcover Evolvulus glomeratus (Blue Daze) - if the plant is upright and clump-forming rather than a trailing mound, it is this Agastache. In containers, it grows by sending new stems up from the root crown, forming a tight cluster that can be sliced into 2-3 rooted 'plugs' with a sharp knife the following spring. Moderate feeder for a mid-summer phosphorus boost, but can get tall and top-heavy if overfed - every 3-4 weeks is plenty. In a fabric-bag soil mix, use the balanced recipe (soil plus equal parts peat moss and perlite) rather than the tropical or desert-native extremes.
